spec_match.rationale: Now calls the exact current surface: Translator.availability({sourceLanguage,targetLanguage}) on the global Translator, and renders the returned enum verbatim. Previously it probed the removed window.ai.translator.capabilities()/languagePairAvailable() namespace and, when that was absent (always, on Chrome 152), fabricated a hard-coded 'readily'/'after-download' guess from a European-language list. Verified in Chrome 152 via chrome-devtools-mcp: real Translator.availability({en,fr}) === 'downloadable' and the page now shows 'downloadable' for the same pair.

interactive.rationale: Two selects, swap, check, plus 36 matrix cells that are now real <button>s — each individually activatable by pointer and keyboard, each re-checking its own pair.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Concept lede matches the feature-index promise on key terms (after, common, download, language, matrix, pair, readily, source, target).

edge_cases.rationale: Four real states are distinguished and none is invented: available / downloadable / downloading / unavailable each get their own badge and advice, an unrecognised non-error string is shown verbatim rather than collapsed into unsupported, a thrown error is surfaced as error:<Name>, and an absent API renders an explicit 'Translator API not present' panel naming the real requirements (desktop Chrome 138+/Edge 148+, ~22GB free, 16GB+ RAM, 4+ cores; not Android/iOS) instead of guessing a result.

references.rationale: Page includes the required chromestatus.com/feature/5172811302961152 link in a references section.

design_system.rationale: All colours come via 79 CSS-variable references, no raw hex, no button background override without a colour override, and not a static-card pattern.

openQuestions.title: Show download progress when a pair is downloadable
openQuestions.detail: availability() deliberately does not download. The natural next concept is a gesture-gated Translator.create() with a monitor(m) callback listening for 'downloadprogress', showing real percentage and the NotAllowedError path when create() is called without a user gesture. The code sample on the page now documents this contract but nothing on the page exercises it.

openQuestions.title: Matrix auto-checks 36 pairs on load, serially
openQuestions.detail: buildMatrix() awaits checkAvailability for every cell in sequence at load. It is correct and cheap today because availability() is local, but it is 36 serial awaits before the grid settles and there is no loading state for the grid as a whole. Consider Promise.all with a per-cell pending state, or defer to first interaction.

summary: API-currency fix (bead 0yr). The page claimed a language pair was 'readily' available by guessing from a hard-coded European-language list whenever the removed window.ai.translator namespace was absent - which is always, on any current Chrome. Chrome 152 reports 'downloadable' for the same pair. That is the contradictory-capability-state and stale-capability-vocabulary anti-regression pair, shipped together, on a page whose entire job is reporting availability. Now calls Translator.availability() and prints what it returns, including unknown values verbatim and an honest no-API panel. Fixed in the same pass: 36 div-onclick matrix cells became named, keyboard-operable buttons, and touch tap targets reach 44px. Verified in Chrome 152 with chrome-devtools-mcp on desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740 DPR3: 0 console messages, 0 horizontal overflow, contrast 20.44/12.4/5.17, route gate PASS.

guidanceConsulted.query: feature detect built-in AI availability and degrade honestly when model unavailable
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: MANDATORY: access the Translator API exclusively via the global Translator interface; DO NOT use or check the deprecated window.ai.translator namespace. availability(options) returns exactly 'available' | 'downloadable' | 'downloading' | 'unavailable'; pass the identical options object to availability() and create(); 'downloadable'/'downloading' + create() strictly requires a user gesture or it rejects with NotAllowedError; provide a monitor(m) downloadprogress callback.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied. Replaced the window.ai.translator.capabilities()/languagePairAvailable() probe and its fabricated 'readily'/'after-download' heuristic with Translator.availability({sourceLanguage,targetLanguage}); adopted the four-value enum in the lede, legend, matrix, badges and advice; rewrote the code sample to show the shared options object, the user-gesture requirement, NotAllowedError, and the downloadprogress monitor.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: chrome-devtools-mcp, Chrome 152. Before: page rendered 'en -> fr: readily (simulated - API not available in this browser)' while Translator.availability({en,fr}) returned 'downloadable' in the same page context. After: page renders 'en -> fr: downloadable' and document contains no window.ai probe (probesWindowAi=false). Screenshots /tmp/0yr-lang-pair-BEFORE.png and /tmp/0yr-lang-pair-AFTER-desktop.png.

guidanceConsulted.query: keyboard accessible interactive grid cells with accessible names and visible focus
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic HTML for activatable controls so they are focusable and operable by keyboard; give every control a programmatic accessible name; keep visible focus; announce state changes non-visually.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied. The 36 clickable matrix cells were <div onclick> - unreachable by keyboard and unnamed. They are now <button type=button> with an aria-label re-written on every state update ('EN to FR: downloadable'), a :focus-visible outline, and the result panel is role=status aria-live=polite so the glyph-only state (checkmark / down-arrow / cross / bang) has a text equivalent.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: chrome-devtools-mcp, Chrome 152: cell-en-fr tagName=BUTTON, tabbable=true, aria-label='EN to FR: downloadable'; 38 buttons on the page, 0 without an accessible name.

guidanceConsulted.query: adequate tap targets on touch without making a dense desktop data grid oversized
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Touch pointers need roughly a 44px minimum target; do not apply the same minimum to fine pointers where it wastes space.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied via @media (pointer: coarse) { .m-cell { min-height: 2.75rem } } so the matrix stays dense for mouse users.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: mobile 360x740 DPR3 touch: cell 36x44, coarsePointer=true, 0px horizontal overflow. desktop 1280x800: cell 102x30, coarsePointer=false, 0px horizontal overflow.
